summary: Generic, dialect-agnostic write operations and per-dialect index-existence SQL. Contains the identifier allowlist validator, dtype coercion (including optional MountainashDtype bridging), rename (build_rename_sql with an Exasol RENAME TABLE branch), additive add_columns, and the generic upsert dispatcher with three SQL families: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT, MERGE INTO (Oracle-specific alias and parenthesised ON handling), and MySQL ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE guarded by a fail-closed unique-index preflight. Index-existence SQL generators cover duckdb, sqlite, motherduck, postgres, mysql, mssql, oracle and singlestore.
extension_points: Pure build_*_sql builders accept an explicit dialect so new dialects can be golden-tested without a live connection
Dialects needing different semantics register a hook on DialectSpec instead of editing the generic path
lifecycle_notes: _generic_upsert follows a documented 12-step validation precedence; warnings are emitted only after all validation and preflight succeed
An UPDATE upsert with an empty update set degrades to insert-or-ignore with a warning
add_columns issues one ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN per missing column and is not atomic across columns
documentation_hooks: Upsert family per dialect and conflict_action semantics (UPDATE / NOTHING)
update_condition predicate grammar and MySQL limitation
MySQL preflight rejection cases (multiple unique indexes, prefix/functional index, column mismatch, nullable keys)
Identifier allowlist: simple identifiers only; dotted names are rejected
risks: motherduck_list_tables is defined but referenced nowhere in src or tests (dead code)
Module docstring lists _format_qualified_table as a helper; the function exists but is unused
ON DUPLICATE KEY uses VALUES(col), deprecated on MySQL 8.0.20+; tested against MariaDB
Error messages recommend an upsert_hook override, but no dialect registers one
add_columns is not concurrency-safe (single-process preflight, then per-column ALTER)
open_questions: Remove motherduck_list_tables and _format_qualified_table, or wire them into dispatch?
